encounters.cc: Evaluation of chronic fatigue and increased susceptibility to respiratory infections.

lines: Evaluation of chronic fatigue and increased susceptibility to respiratory infections.

He reports feeling generally well between episodes but describes a history of intermittent joint pain, particularly in the hips and knees, which flares unpredictably and is sometimes associated with low-grade fever.
He denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or weight loss.
He has been hospitalized several times since childhood for unexplained episodes of severe limb pain and abdominal discomfort, often requiring intravenous fluids and analgesics.
He reports that these episodes have become less frequent over the past few years, but he still occasionally experiences milder bouts of bone pain.
He has not seen a primary care physician in several years.
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
His past medical history is notable for chronic anemia and a remote history of bacterial meningitis during childhood.
Vaccination records are incomplete, but he recalls receiving “extra shots” as a child.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
On physical exam, his temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 108/64 mmHg, and pulse is 92/min.
He appears thin but in no acute distress.
Conjunctivae are pale, and sclerae are anicteric.
Abdominal examination reveals no hepatosplenomegaly, and the spleen is not palpable.

encounters.cc: Intermittent difficulty swallowing solid foods and sensation of food getting stuck in chest for 6 months.

lines: Intermittent difficulty swallowing solid foods and sensation of food getting stuck in chest for 6 months.

This 19-year-old male with sickle cell anemia (HbSS) and asplenia, last evaluated in Hematology three months ago for fatigue, now presents to Gastroenterology with a 6-month history of intermittent difficulty swallowing solid foods and a sensation that food is getting stuck in his chest.
He denies any weight loss, gastrointestinal bleeding, or changes in bowel habits.
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
He takes albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
His vital signs are within normal limits
There is no lymphadenopathy or abdominal tenderness.
His skin examination reveals several patches of dry, scaly skin consistent with eczema.
Biopsy of the esophageal mucosa reveals significant eosinophilic infiltration.
An upper endoscopy is performed, which shows multiple concentric rings and linear furrows in the esophagus.

encounters.cc: Progressive left hip pain over 3 weeks, worse with weight-bearing.

lines: Progressive left hip pain over 3 weeks, worse with weight-bearing.
The patient with known bilateral femoral head avascular necrosis returns with hip pain.
He describes the pain as dull and constant, with occasional sharp exacerbations.
The pain worsens with weight-bearing activities and improves with rest.
He denies any recent trauma or injury.
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
His medical history is significant for sickle cell disease, for which he has been hospitalized twice in the past year for vaso-occlusive crises.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
On physical examination, the patient has a reduced range of motion in the left hip, particularly with internal rotation and abduction.
There is no erythema, warmth, or swelling over the joint.
Initial plain radiographs of the hip are unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of sharp left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to left shoulder after transatlantic flight.

lines: Sudden onset of sharp left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to left shoulder after transatlantic flight.

The patient is a 21-year-old male with sickle cell anemia (HbSS genotype) and history of eosinophilic esophagitis and bilateral femoral head avascular necrosis who presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of sharp, left upper quadrant abdominal pain that started 12 hours ago during a transatlantic flight.
He describes the pain as constant and radiating to his left shoulder.
He also reports feeling fatigued and having dark urine since the onset of the pain.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
His past medical history is significant for mild asthma.
He denies any recent trauma or surgery.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
On examination, his temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, and respiratory rate is 18/min.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness to palpation in the left upper quadrant with no rebound or guarding.
- Peripheral smear: Presence of "bite cells" and "schistocytes"

encounters.cc: Fatigue and shortness of breath for two weeks following recent splenectomy.

lines: Fatigue and shortness of breath for two weeks following recent splenectomy.

The patient is a 21-year-old male with sickle cell anemia (HbSS) and asplenia status post splenectomy two months prior for atraumatic rupture, returning for outpatient hematology follow-up with two weeks of fatigue and shortness of breath.
He denies fever, chills, or recent infections.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
He has a history of sickle cell disease and reports several episodes of acute chest syndrome in the past.
His vaccinations are up to date.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
On physical examination, his temperature is 37.2°C, blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
- Peripheral smear: Presence of Howell-Jolly bodies

encounters.cc: Painful erection lasting 6 hours without sexual activity or trauma.

lines: Painful erection lasting 6 hours without sexual activity or trauma.
The patient is a 21-year-old male with sickle cell anemia (HbSS genotype) and status post splenectomy six months ago secondary to atraumatic rupture who presents with his current symptoms.
He denies any sexual activity, trauma, or illicit drug use prior to the onset of his symptoms.
He reports that he has not had any recent sickle cell crises.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
His past medical history is significant for sickle cell anemia.
He takes hydroxyurea and folic acid.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
His vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, the penis is fully erect, tender to palpation, and there is no evidence of trauma.
The testes and abdomen are unremarkable on examination.

encounters.cc: Painful erection persisting for 6 hours, similar to prior episode that resolved spontaneously.

lines: Painful erection persisting for 6 hours, similar to prior episode that resolved spontaneously.

The patient is a 22-year-old male with sickle cell anemia (HbSS genotype) and history of similar presentation in July 2022 who presents to the emergency department with a painful erection that has persisted for 6 hours.
He denies any sexual activity or trauma to the genital area.
He reports that he has had similar, but less severe episodes in the past that resolved spontaneously.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Ischemic priapism secondary to sickle cell disease (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
His past medical history is significant for sickle cell disease.
He takes for which he is on hydroxyurea and folic acid.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
He appears to be in moderate distress due to pain.
On examination, his penis is fully erect, tender to palpation, and there is no evidence of trauma.
His abdomen is soft and non-tender, and there are no inguinal lymphadenopathies.

encounters.cc: Acute right hip pain, high fever, and inability to bear weight.

lines: Acute right hip pain, high fever, and inability to bear weight.

This 23-year-old male with HbSS sickle cell anemia, status post splenectomy for atraumatic rupture, and known bilateral femoral head avascular necrosis presents with acute right hip pain, fever, and an inability to bear weight.
He denies trauma, recent illness, infections, or skin wounds.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Ischemic priapism secondary to sickle cell disease (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Status post splenectomy (secondary to atraumatic splenic rupture)
- Avascular necrosis of bilateral femoral heads
- History of acute chest syndrome (multiple episodes)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Maternal grandmother with asthma and environmental allergies
- Older brother with sickle cell disease
On examination, the joint is swollen, erythematous, and tender with severely restricted motion.
Laboratory testing reveals a WBC count of 15,200/μL, ESR of 80 mm/hr, and CRP of 115 mg/L.
Joint aspiration yields turbid synovial fluid with 95,000 WBCs/μL (90% neutrophils) and no crystals or organisms on Gram stain.
The patient is admitted and started on empiric IV antibiotics.
